description: This bar chart illustrates the average performance and token usage of CoUT and baseline methods for four large reasoning models over four benchmarks. The chart features two distinct clusters of bars corresponding to two different metrics, each with its own vertical value axis. The left vertical axis, labeled "Accuracy (%)", uses a linear scale ranging from 70 to 100 with tick marks at intervals of 5. The right vertical axis, labeled "Token Count", uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 800 with tick marks at intervals of 100. The horizontal axis does not have a single label but separates the data into the two metric clusters. Within each cluster, there are four bars representing different methods, identified by a legend at the bottom: CoT (red), CoD (orange), CCoT (light blue), and CoUT (green). In the left cluster representing Accuracy, the exact values are annotated above each bar: CoT is the tallest at 91.19, followed by CCoT at 88.50, CoUT at 88.40, and CoD is the shortest at 80.89. In the right cluster representing Token Count, the annotated values are: CoT is the tallest at 676.85, followed by CoD at 534.24, CCoT at 445.91, and CoUT is the shortest at 354.46. The bars within each group are arranged in the order presented in the legend rather than being sorted by numerical value, and every bar is visually emphasized with its exact numerical value printed directly above it.
